intended_object: The coordinate ring, written in polynomial coordinates, of the overlap D₊(X_i) ∩ D₊(X_j) of two standard affine charts of projective space over R. It is the ring R[x_k : k ≠ i][x_j⁻¹], where x_k stands for X_k/X_i. This reading comes from the docstring and from the equivalence `standardChartPolynomialOverlapEquiv` proved right after it.
explanation: The body is `Localization.Away (X j)`, taken in `MvPolynomial {k // k ≠ i} R`. This polynomial ring is the presentation of the i-th standard chart, R[X_k/X_i : k ≠ i]. Inverting the variable that stands for X_j/X_i gives the coordinate ring of the overlap of the two charts, which is exactly what the docstring says. The library then proves an R-algebra isomorphism with the degree-zero homogeneous localization at X_i·X_j (`standardChartPolynomialOverlapEquiv`), which confirms this reading. The definition is just Mathlib's general `Localization.Away` applied to a specific ring. R is an arbitrary commutative ring and ι an arbitrary index type, so nothing is narrower than it needs to be. Mathlib has no separate declaration for this particular ring.
